sections.english: Injustice is sin. Universal nature has constituted rational creatures for the sake of each other: to help each other, then, as is deserved, and never to harm each other. Someone who transgresses this is clearly guilty of sin against the most venerable of gods.
sections.chinese: 不正义即是罪。宇宙之本性将理性造物造为彼此之缘故而存：彼此按其所应得而相助，而永不相害。违犯此道者，显然犯了亵渎那最庄严神圣之罪。

sections.english: Lying, too, is a sin against the same goddess: her name is Truth, and she is the original cause of all that is true. The conscious liar sins to the extent that his deceit causes injustice: the unconscious liar to the extent that he is out of tune with the nature of the Whole and out of order with the universe.
sections.chinese: 说谎，亦是对此一同样之女神的罪过：她之名乃是真理，且她是一切真实之事物之元始原因。有意识之说谎者，其罪在其欺诓导致不正义之程度：无意识之说谎者，其罪在其与宇宙整体之本性失和、与宇宙之秩序脱轨。

sections.english: Moreover, the pursuit of pleasure as a good and the avoidance of pain as an evil constitutes sin. Someone like that must inevitably and frequently blame universal Nature for unfair distribution as between bad men and good, since bad men are often deep in pleasures and the possessions which make for pleasure, while good men meet with pain and what causes pain.
sections.chinese: 再者，以追求逸乐为善、逃避痛苦为恶，此亦构成罪过。那般行事之人，必然且频繁地责备宇宙之自然分配不公——竟厚于恶人而薄于善人，因恶人常沉浸于逸乐及产生逸乐之财物中，而善人则遭逢痛苦及引发痛苦之事。

sections.english: Further, anyone who fears pain will also at times be afraid of some future event in the world, and that is immediate sin. And a man who pursues pleasure will not hold back from injustice — an obvious sin. Those who wish to follow Nature and share her mind must themselves be indifferent to those pairs of opposites in which Nature is also indifferent.
sections.chinese: 此外，凡惧怕痛苦者，亦有之时会惧怕世间某未来之事变，而这即是当行之罪。而一追求逸乐之人，亦必不会在行不义之时收敛——这是昭然之罪。凡愿追寻自然、与自然之心意共契者，必须于自然同样漠然相视之那些对立两面，自身也同样漠然不动。

sections.english: By 'universal Nature treating these things indifferently' I mean that they happen impartially by cause and effect to all that comes into being and owes its being to the fulfilment of an original impulse of Providence. Under this impulse Providence set out from a first premise to establish the present order of the universe.
sections.chinese: 我所谓「宇宙之自然对这些漠然处之」，意即：它们藉由因果而平等无偏地发生于一切生成之物上——而这一切生成之物其存有皆源于天意之元初冲动之实现。在这一冲动之下，天意自第一前提出发，建立了宇宙当前之秩序。

sections.english: These will suffice: the present certainty of judgement, the present social action, the present disposition well content with any effect of an external cause.
sections.chinese: 如此便已足够：当下判断之确然，当下之社会性行动，以及当下欣然接纳任何外来原因效应之性情倾向。

sections.english: Erase the print of imagination, stop impulse, quench desire: keep your directing mind its own master.
sections.chinese: 抹除想象之印迹，止住冲动，熄灭欲望：令你主导之心灵做自己之主宰。

sections.english: Irrational creatures share in one animate soul, and rational creatures partake in one intelligent soul: just as there is one earth for all the things of earth, and one light to see by, one air to breathe for all of us who have sight and life. All things which share some common quality tend to their own kind.
sections.chinese: 非理性之造物共有一有生魂灵，理性之造物则共有一智性灵魂：正如地之一切土物有一共同之大地，所有具视觉与生命者皆赖同一光以视物、同一空气以呼吸。凡共有某种同类品质之物，皆倾向其同宗之类属。

sections.english: Look then at what is happening now. Only the intelligent creatures have now forgotten that urge to be unified with each other: only here will you see no confluence. They may run from it, but nevertheless they are overtaken: such is the power of nature. Look carefully and you will see what I mean. You will sooner find something earthy not touching earth than a man severed from man.
sections.chinese: 再看现在正发生之事。唯具智性之造物如今忘却了彼此合一之冲动：唯在此处，你看不到汇聚。他们或会逃离，然而自然终将追上他们：此自然之力如是。仔细观看，你将明白我所指之意。你找到不与大地相接之土物，要比找到一个与人隔绝之人来的更容易。

sections.english: Man, god, and the universe all bear fruit, each in its own due season. No matter if common use confines the strict sense of 'bearing fruit' to vines and the like. Reason too has its fruit, both universal and particular: other things grow from it which share its own nature.
sections.chinese: 人、神、宇宙皆结其果实，各在其当有之季节。不论惯常用法是否将「结果实」这层严格之意义仅限于藤蔓之类。理性亦有其果实，既有普遍者，亦有特殊者：其他与之同性之物皆因此生长而出。

sections.english: If you can, show them the better way. If you cannot, remember that this is why you have the gift of kindness. The gods too are kind to such people, and in their benevolence even help them achieve some ends — health, wealth, fame. You can do it too. Or tell me — who is stopping you?
sections.chinese: 若你能够，便将更善之路示与他们。若你不能，便记住：这正是你被赋予仁善这一禀赋的因由。诸神亦是以仁善待这般人等，且在其仁慈中甚而帮助他们达致某些目的——健康、财富、声名。你亦能做到。否则请告诉我——谁拦阻了你？

sections.english: Work. Don't work as a miserable drudge, or in any expectation of pity or admiration. One aim only: action or inaction as civic cause demands.
sections.chinese: 去工作。勿如一名悲惨之苦役那般工作，亦勿怀着任何博取同情或钦羡的期待去工作。只有一个目标：行动或不行动，均视公民事业之所需而定。

sections.english: Today I escaped from all bothering circumstances — or rather I threw them out. They were nothing external, but inside me, just my own judgements.
sections.chinese: 今日我从一切烦扰之处境中得脱——或更确切说，我将它们逐出。它们并非外物，而全在己内，仅为己之判断而已。

sections.english: All things are the same: familiar in experience, transient in time, sordid in substance. Everything now is as it was in the days of those we have buried.
sections.chinese: 一切皆相同：经验中悉为熟见，时间中皆属短暂，实质上尽是污浊。如今之每一事，恰如我们已埋葬的那些先人的代时所是一般。

sections.english: Mere things stand isolated outside our doors, with no knowledge or report of themselves. What then reports on them? Our directing mind.
sections.chinese: 赤裸之物事孤独立在我们的门扉之外，对其自身毫无知识、亦无信息。那么是何物在报告它们呢？吾辈之主导心灵。

sections.english: Good or ill for the rational social being lies not in feeling but in action: just as also his own virtue or vice shows not in what he feels, but in what he does.
sections.chinese: 理性而社会性之存在者，其善与恶不在于感受，而在于行动：正如其自身之德性与邪行并非显现于其感受之中，而乃显现于其所行之事中。

sections.english: A stone thrown in the air: nothing bad for it on the way down or good for it on the way up.
sections.chinese: 一块抛向空中之石：下落之途于它无坏，上升之道于它亦无好。

sections.english: Penetrate into their directing minds, and you will see what sort of critics you fear — and what poor critics they are of themselves.
sections.chinese: 穿透他们之主导心灵，便将看出你所畏惧的是何等样之评判者——而他们裁判起自身来，又是何等蹩脚。

sections.english: All things are in a process of change. You yourself are subject to constant alteration and gradual decay. So too is the whole universe.
sections.chinese: 万物皆处于变化之流程中。你自身亦在恒常之变易与逐渐之凋朽中。整个宇宙亦是如此。

sections.english: You should leave another's wrong where it lies.
sections.chinese: 你当将别人之过错，留在其所在之处。

sections.english: The termination of an activity, the pause when an impulse or judgement is finished — this is a sort of death, but no harm in it. Turn now to the stages of your life — childhood, say, adolescence, prime, old age. Here too each change a death: anything fearful there?
sections.chinese: 活动之终结，一冲动或判断完结之时之暂停——此亦是一种死亡，但于中并无伤害。现在转而返观你生命之各阶段——童年，譬如，少年，壮岁，暮年。其中每一变化皆是一种死亡：其间有什么可畏吗？

sections.english: Hurry to your own directing mind, to the mind of the Whole, and to the mind of this particular man. To your own mind, to make its understanding just; to the mind of the Whole, to recall what you are part of; to this man's mind, to see whether there is ignorance or design — and at the same time to reflect that he is your kinsman.
sections.chinese: 疾赴你自身之主导心灵，赴宇宙整体之心灵，以及赴此一特定人之心灵。赴己之心灵，以令其理解正当公允；赴整体之心灵，以铭记你所附属之部分是什么；赴此人之心灵，以查看他究竟是出于无知还是蓄意——同时亦反思，他乃是你的同源之人。

sections.english: Just as you yourself are a complementary part of a social system, so too your every action should complement a life of social principle. If any action of yours, then, does not have direct or indirect relation to the social end, it pulls your life apart and destroys its unity. It is a kind of sedition, like a man in a popular assembly who stands apart and acts on his own.
sections.chinese: 正如你自身是一个社会体系中的互补之部分，你之每一行动也当弥补成全一种具有社会性原则之生命。若你任何之行动，没有直接或间接关联于社会性之目标，它便会在撕开你之生命，毁坏其整全之统一。这是一类叛乱——如同在公众集会中，一人自行单独站立一旁，独行其是。

sections.english: Children's tantrums and toys, 'tiny spirits carrying corpses' — the Underworld in the Odyssey strikes more real!
sections.chinese: 孩童之闹脾气与玩偶，所谓「渺小之灵魂携带着死尸」——《奥德赛》中之冥界反倒显得更为真实！

sections.english: Go straight to the qualifying cause and examine it separately from the material element. Then establish the maximum time for which this individual thing thus qualified can by its nature subsist.
sections.chinese: 径直走向那定性之原因，将其与物质之元素分开来细加检审。然后，确定此一个别之事物在如此之定性下、能依其本性而存续的最长时间。

sections.english: You have endured innumerable troubles by not leaving your directing mind to do the work it was made for. But enough.
sections.chinese: 你已因不让你之主导心灵做它本被造为去做之功，而忍受了数不尽之烦扰。然，此事可以休矣。

sections.english: When another blames you or hates you, or people voice similar criticisms, go to their souls, penetrate inside and see what sort of people they are. You will realize that there is no need to be racked with anxiety that they should hold any particular opinion about you. But you should still be kind to them. They are by nature your friends, and the gods too help them in various ways — by dreams, by oracles — to win what they set their hearts on.
sections.chinese: 当别人责备你或恨恶你，或有人说出类似之批评时，请走进他们的灵魂，穿透进去，看看他们是何等样人。你将明白，无需为他们对你怀有怎样的意见而忧心如焚。但你仍应对他们友善。他们从本性上便是你的朋友，而诸神也以种种方式帮助他们——通过梦境、通过神谕——去赢获那些他们心之所倾的东西。

sections.english: The universal cause is a torrent, sweeping everything in its stream. So, man, what does that mean for you? Do what nature requires at this moment. Start straight away, if that is in your power: don't look over your shoulder to see if people will know. Don't hope for Plato's utopian republic, but be content with the smallest step forward, and regard even that result as no mean achievement.
sections.chinese: 宇宙之原因是一道湍流，携卷一切于其流中。那么，人啊，这于你又意味着什么呢？于此刻做自然所要求之事。如果此事在你的权能之内，即刻开始：莫回首张望看别人是否会知道。莫寄望于柏拉图之乌托邦，而满足于微小之脚步渐进，且将此即便是如此之结果，也不视作微不足道之成就。

sections.english: Take a view from above — look at the thousands of flocks and herds, the thousands of human ceremonies, every sort of voyage in storm or calm, the range of creation, combination, and extinction. Consider too the lives once lived by others long before you, the lives that will be lived after you, the lives lived now among foreign tribes: how many have never even heard your name, how many will quickly forget it, how many praise you now but will very soon turn to blame.
sections.chinese: 从高处俯瞰——看那千千万万之畜群与牧队、千千万万之人间仪式、各种在风暴或平静中的航行、创造与结合与绝灭之百态万象。也想想那些远在你之前、别人曾经活过之生命，那些将在你之后被活出之生命，此刻正在异族部落中被活出之生命：多少人甚至从未听说过你的名字，多少人转眼便将忘记它，多少人此刻在赞誉你，转眼便会转而责骂。

sections.english: Calm acceptance of what comes from a cause outside yourself, and justice in all activity of your own causation. In other words, impulse and action fulfilled in that social conduct which is an expression of your own nature.
sections.chinese: 对外因所来之一切安然接纳，对己身所起之因的一切行为持守公道。换言之，由冲动与行动在那表达了你自身本性之社会行为中得以完成。

sections.english: You can strip away many unnecessary troubles which lie wholly in your own judgement. And you will immediately make large and wide room for yourself by grasping the whole universe in your thought, contemplating the eternity of time, and reflecting on the rapid change of each thing in every part — how brief the gap from birth to dissolution, how yawning the gulf of time before your birth, and an equal infinity after your dissolution.
sections.chinese: 你可以剥去许多全然存于你自己判断中不必要的烦恼。而你立即便能为自己腾出广大宽阔之空间——只要以你的思想把握整个宇宙，凝思时间之永恒，并反思每物在每个部分中何其迅速的变化：从出生到消亡之间隔何其短暂，你出生之前时间之鸿渊何其广袤，而你消亡之后另有一同等之无穷。

sections.english: All that you see will soon perish; those who witness this perishing will soon perish themselves. Die in extreme old age or die before your time — it will all be the same.
sections.chinese: 你所见之一切，即将消亡殆尽；那些见证这消亡的人，很快他们自身亦将消亡。于极老极寿之年死去，或于应有时刻之前死去——终究都是一样。

sections.english: What are the directing minds of these people? What are they set on, what governs their likes and values? Train yourself to look at their souls naked. When they think that their blame will hurt or their praise advantage, what a conceit that is!
sections.chinese: 这些人的主导之心智是怎样的？他们究竟所倾心者为何，是什么在统御着他们的好恶与价值？自己训练自己，去观看他们赤裸的魂灵。当他们自认其责斥能伤害、其称赞能施惠时，这是何等之自大妄想！

sections.english: Loss is nothing more than change. Universal nature delights in change, and all that flows from nature happens for the good. Similar things have happened from time everlasting, and there will be more such to eternity. So why do you say that everything has always happened for the bad and always will, that all those gods have clearly been powerless to correct this, and that the world has been condemned to the grip of a never-ending evil?
sections.chinese: 丧失不过是变化而已。宇宙之自然以变为乐，而一切自自然流出者皆因善而发生。类似之事自永恒以来便一直在发生，且将有更多此类之事直至永恒。你为何要说一切向来且必定是朝着坏的方向发生，说那无数之神明显然无力纠正此点，而世界已被定谳为一永无止歇的恶所钳制？

sections.english: The rotting of the base material of everything. Water, dust, bones, stench. Again: marble is a mere deposit in the earth, gold and silver mere sediments; your clothing is animal hair, your purple is fish blood; and so on with all else. And the vital spirit is just the same, changing from this to that.
sections.chinese: 一切之基质材料皆在腐坏：水、尘、骨、恶臭。再如：大理石不过是地中一层积沉，金银不过是些沉渣；你之衣袍是兽之毛发，你的紫袍是鱼之血；其他一切，莫不如是。而那生气之灵也相同，由此至彼不断变去。

sections.english: Enough of this miserable way of life, enough of grumbling and aping! Why are you troubled? What is new in this? What is it that drives you mad? The cause? Then face it. Or rather the material? Then face that. Apart from cause and material there is nothing. But you should even now, late though it is, make yourself a simpler and better man in your dealings with the gods.
sections.chinese: 这种可怜悲惨之生活方式可以罢了，那牢骚抱怨、那效颦学舌也可以罢了！你为何烦恼？此事中有什么是新的？是什么在驱使你疯狂？原因吗？去直面它。或是那物质吗？也去直面它。离开原因与物质，便再无一物。但即在此刻——虽已甚迟——你也当使自己在那与诸神的关系中成为一较简朴、更善好的人。

sections.english: If he did wrong, the harm is to himself. But perhaps he did not do wrong.
sections.chinese: 若他做了错事，其伤害乃是他自己承受。但也许，他并未做错。

sections.english: Either all things flow from one intelligent source and supervene as in one coordinated body, so the part should not complain at what happens in the interest of the whole — or all is atoms, and nothing more than present stew and future dispersal. Why then are you troubled? Say to your directing mind: 'Are you dead? Are you corrupt? Are you playing the hypocrite? Have you become a beast? Do you herd with the rest and share their food?'
sections.chinese: 要么万物皆从一智性之源而流出，并如在一个协调一体中互相续随——如此，部分便不应抱怨那为整体利益而发生的事——要么一切皆不过是原子，不超过当下这一锅乱炖及将来之离散。那么，你又为何烦恼？对你之主导心灵说：「你是死了吗？你朽烂了吗？你在假扮吗？你已变成了野兽？你和那群人混在一起分享他们的饲料了吗？」

sections.english: Epicurus says: 'In my illness my conversations were not about the sufferings of my poor body, and I did not prattle on to my visitors in this vein, but I continued to discuss the cardinal principles of natural philosophy, with particular reference to this very point, how the mind shares in such disturbances of the flesh but is nonetheless immune to distress and can preserve its own proper good.'
sections.chinese: 伊壁鸩鲁说：「我病中之时，我的谈话并不围绕着我那可怜躯体之诸般痛苦，亦未就此絮叨于访客，而是继续讨论自然哲学之根本原则，尤其着力于是乎于此一要点：即心智虽涉身在此等肉体之扰乱中，却如何不受苦恼之扰，并能持守其自身本有之善好。」

sections.english: Whenever you are offended at someone's lack of shame, you should immediately ask yourself: 'So is it possible for there to be no shameless people in the world?' It is not possible. Do not then ask for the impossible. This person is just one of the shameless inevitably existing in the world. Have the same thought ready for the rogue, the traitor, every sort of offender.
sections.chinese: 当你为某人之无廉耻而感到不快时，你当立即自问：「那么，世间可能全无无耻之徒乎？」那是不可能的。既如此，便不要奢求那不可能之事。此人只是那些势必存在于世间之无耻之徒中的一个。对于无赖、背叛者和各类冒犯之徒，也当备有同样之念。

sections.english: Anyway, where is the harm or surprise in the ignorant behaving as the ignorant do? Think about it. Should you not rather blame yourself, for not anticipating that this man would make this error? Your reason gave you the resource to reckon this mistake likely from this man, yet you forgot and are now surprised that he went wrong.
sections.chinese: 无论如何，无知者所为正如无知者之所为，这之中又有何伤害或意外？仔细想想。难道你不应更该责怪你自己，因你未曾预料到此人会犯此等错误？你之理性已给了你借此量出此人极可能犯此谬误的凭具，然你却忘了，如见却对他行差错步而感到愕然。
